speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature 36.8°C (98.2°F), Blood Pressure 135/85 mmHg, Heart Rate 82 bpm, Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min. speaker: Doctor
text: Given the extremely high white blood cell count and the presence of Auer rods, do you have a history of chemotherapy or any known blood disorders? I need to confirm if you have experienced any recent bone pain or bleeding episodes to finalize the assessment.

text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. No known blood disorders or cancer history in the family. Social history: Retired teacher, lives with his wife. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of Auer rods alongside your high white blood cell count and low platelets strongly suggests Acute Myeloid Leukemia. I will now proceed to confirm this suspicion with specific genetic testing. REQUEST TEST: Bone Marrow Biopsy and Cytogenetic Analysis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bone Marrow Biopsy: Hypercellular marrow (95% cellularity) with >30% myeloblasts. Cytogenetic Analysis: Confirmed t(8;21)(q22;q22) translocation (RUNX1-RUNX1T1 fusion gene). Flow Cytometry: Blasts are positive for CD13, CD33, CD117, and MPO. Diagnosis confirmed as Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML), M2 subtype (AML with maturation).

speaker: Doctor
text: The bone marrow results and genetic markers confirm a diagnosis of Acute Myeloid Leukemia, specifically the M2 subtype with the t(8;21) translocation. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML), M2 subtype.
